newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahraini court to rule on some plot suspects.
newsitem.headline: Bahraini court to rule on some plot suspects.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court will on Wednesday pass verdicts on around 29 people accused of involvement in what officials said was a pro-Iranian attempt to topple the government by force, lawyers said.
"The court will pass verdicts on four groups consisting of around 29 to 30 suspects," one defence lawyer told Reuters.
Lawyers said the court was trying 81 suspects, 59 of whom were present with the remainder still at large.
"I expect the remaining verdicts to be given on Saturday," the lawyer said.
The trial started in the Gulf Arab state on March 1. Lawyers said some defendants could face the death penalty if convicted.

The defendants are accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Bahrain last June accused Iran of backing an attempt to topple the government by force. Iran denied the charge.

Members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protects, bombings, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from Bahrain's largely Sunni government. At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested.
